chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ṣafwān, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot al-Ẓuhr until the sun had set, while he had already performed al-ʿAṣr. He said: “Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, or my father عليه السلام, used to say: If he is able to perform it before al-Maghrib passes him by, he begins with it; otherwise, he performs al-Maghrib and then performs it.”

key_terms.بَدَأَ بِهَا: he begins with it, meaning he performs the missed Ẓuhr first
key_terms.ثُمَّ صَلَّاهَا: then he performs it, referring to the delayed Ẓuhr salat (prayer)
key_terms.غَرَبَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun set, marking the end of the daytime prayer period
key_terms.نَسِيَ: forgot or failed to remember the obligation in time

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they forgot Ẓuhr until sunset after already praying ʿAṣr?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who forgot the Ẓuhr salat (prayer) until after sunset, having already performed ʿAṣr. If there is enough time to perform the missed Ẓuhr before the time of Maghrib is lost, he should begin with it; otherwise, he should perform Maghrib first and then make up Ẓuhr.
